title: MCP tool-definition digest
pins: The exact digest an MCP tool definition produces in every language. A digest is the material of a TrustPolicy pin, so this is the one value in the package that MUST be byte-identical across implementations: a pin computed against a PHP deployment is pasted into a TypeScript or Python config by an operator who has no way to know the two disagree. Per-language suites cannot see this — each one is perfectly happy digesting its own way.
scope: The tool-definition DIGEST -- the material of a TrustPolicy pin. It does not cover which tools a policy admits, how results are framed, or the transport. A green run means a pin computed in one language validates in another; it says nothing about whether the policy around it is right.

ts.gap: dig-0002, dig-0003 and dig-0007 diverge from the reference and are recorded as `divergence` rather than skipped, because a skip would hide the finding. Two causes, both proven by dumping the pre-hash material: PHP renders an empty map-typed field as `[]` where this language renders `{}` (the same F-3 artefact as rtp-0009), and PHP coerces an absent description to `""` where this language keeps `null`. Consequence: a pin does not transfer between PHP and this language for those shapes. See G-20.

py.gap: Identical to ts, and identical byte-for-byte to ts on all ten rows — the two ports agree with each other and disagree with the reference on the same three. That is itself the useful signal: it is one reference-side artefact plus one coercion choice, not two independent port bugs. See G-20.
